config.title: Nested Routes & Protected Routes

intro.title: Nested Routes & Protected Routes
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple multi-page application with a dashboard that has nested sub-pages and a login-protected profile section. You will learn how to organize routes hierarchically using React Router's nested routing feature and how to restrict access to certain routes based on authentication state. The main technologies involved are React Router components like `Routes`, `Route`, `Outlet`, and custom components for layout and protection. By the end, you'll understand how to structure complex applications and implement basic route guarding for a better user experience.
intro.usecase: Nested routes are essential for organizing complex applications with hierarchical navigation, like e-commerce sites where product categories contain subcategories and individual product pages. Protected routes are critical for securing user-specific areas such as account dashboards, admin panels, or subscription-only content in SaaS applications. In practice, you'll implement these patterns when building user profiles with tabs for settings, orders, and payment methods, or enterprise dashboards with nested analytics sections accessible only to authorized roles. Mastering these concepts lets you create professional applications with proper access control and logical URL structures that reflect the application's information architecture.

objectives: Implement nested route structures using React Router's Route and Outlet components
Configure protected route components that conditionally render content based on authentication state
Construct a navigation component that renders links matching your nested route hierarchy
Initialize and manipulate route parameters within nested route components
Apply programmatic navigation to redirect users from protected routes when unauthenticated
Integrate authentication state management with route protection logic
Render dynamic breadcrumb navigation that reflects the current nested route location

steps.expectedOutcome: The Dashboard component will have both Profile and Settings routes defined as children, enabling nested routing.

steps.title: Create an AuthProvider component with authentication state
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named AuthProvider that uses useState to manage an isAuthenticated state variable (initialized to false). The component should accept children as a prop and return them wrapped in an AuthContext.Provider.
steps.hint: Use useState to create a state variable called isAuthenticated. The AuthProvider component should return children inside an AuthContext.Provider with the authentication state as value.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have an AuthProvider component that manages authentication state and provides it to child components via context.
successCriteria: AuthProvider component is created with useState managing isAuthenticated state and returns children wrapped in AuthContext.Provider
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a component, but it's missing either the useState hook for isAuthenticated or the AuthContext.Provider wrapper.
steps.feedbackWrong: The AuthProvider component is not properly implemented. Make sure to use useState for isAuthenticated and wrap children in AuthContext.Provider.

steps.title: Create a ProtectedRoute component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named ProtectedRoute that takes children and isAuthenticated as props, checks authentication, and returns either the children or a redirect message.
steps.hint: Define a function that accepts props, checks isAuthenticated, and conditionally returns children or a fallback message.
steps.expectedOutcome: A ProtectedRoute component is defined that can conditionally render children based on authentication status.
successCriteria: ProtectedRoute component is created with props for children and isAuthenticated, includes conditional logic, and returns either children or a fallback message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the ProtectedRoute component. Make sure it accepts props, checks isAuthenticated, and returns children when authenticated or a fallback message when not.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ProtectedRoute component is not yet correctly implemented. It should be a functional component that takes children and isAuthenticated props and conditionally returns content.

steps.title: Wrap Dashboard route with ProtectedRoute
steps.instruction: In the App component's Routes section, wrap the Dashboard route element with the ProtectedRoute component.
steps.hint: Replace the element prop of the Dashboard route with <ProtectedRoute><Dashboard /></ProtectedRoute>.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: wrapping a route with a higher-order component
<Route path="/admin" element={<ProtectedRoute><AdminPanel /></ProtectedRoute>} />
steps.expectedOutcome: The Dashboard route is now protected and will only render if authentication passes.
successCriteria: The Dashboard route element is wrapped with the ProtectedRoute component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're wrapping the Dashboard component inside the ProtectedRoute component as the element prop.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Dashboard route is not properly wrapped with ProtectedRoute. Check the syntax for nested JSX elements.
